regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood leads with 18" through Monday, and the big day is Friday with 15". The NWS is calling for more, 29" to 49" Friday through Monday night. A Winter Storm Watch runs Friday through Monday. Sugar Bowl and Palisades are close behind.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler leads with 21" through Monday, peaking Sunday at 13". Expect rain at times heavy and mixed conditions through Thursday, then snow building from Saturday. Cypress Mountain sees only 2" on Sunday, so Whistler is the better bet.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth totals 10" through Monday, with 9" on Friday. The NWS is calling for more, 14" to 26" Friday through Monday night. A Winter Storm Watch runs Friday through Saturday. Strong southwest winds with gusts to 55 mph are likely Friday night.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: Crystal Mountain leads with 7" through Sunday, peaking Saturday at 3". Rain mixes with snow through the weekend, so expect heavy, wet snow at mid elevations. Stevens Pass also totals 7", and Mt. Baker sees 6".

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Killington leads with 8" through Saturday, peaking Thursday at 5". The NWS is calling for more, 6" to 13" Thursday through Friday night. Whiteface follows at 6", and Stowe at 5". Light snow and gusty northerly winds are expected.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a stronger front brings colder air and lower snow levels to the Sierra and northern California ranges around Monday Nov 23, with moderate accumulations likely. Confidence is in its own words moderate.
